name: Surf Air Mobility Inc.

profile.description: Surf Air Mobility operates the largest commuter airline network in the United States (via Southern Airways Express and Mokulele) plus an on-demand private charter marketplace, and is developing SurfOS, an AI-enabled aviation operating software suite built with Palantir, along with regional aircraft electrification technology. FY2025 revenue was $106.6M with a net loss of $110.6M. Q2 2026 revenue was $29.5M (+8% YoY), and management reaffirmed FY2026 guidance of $128-138M revenue and a $25-30M adjusted EBITDA loss. CEO Deanna White has led the company since 2024.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): Surf Air's main transformation was the 2023 acquisition of Southern Airways, which lifted revenue from $11.8M in FY2021 to $106.6M in FY2025, followed by a 2025-2026 pivot toward charter (charter revenue +101% YoY in Q2 2026) and exits from unprofitable scheduled routes [1][3]. This is consolidation and restructuring rather than a proven product breakthrough. AI Deployment (1/2): SurfOS, an AI-enabled product suite developed with an expanded Palantir relationship, targets commercial rollout in 2026; management credits it with crew scheduling, dispatch, and maintenance digitization gains, but no quantified savings or external revenue are disclosed [5][6]. Market Share (1/2): Surf Air describes itself as the largest US commuter airline by scheduled departures, a meaningful niche position but not category leadership with share-gain data [1]. Pipeline (1/2): SurfOS commercial rollout and the electrified Cessna Caravan program are named, but electrification lacks firm certification and revenue timelines [5][6]. R&D Intensity (1/1): R&D of $10.3M equals roughly 6.6% of revenue (FMP), far above typical airline R&D spend [4].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Surf Air's stated aim of making regional air travel accessible, technology-enabled, and ultimately electrified is clear but not yet validated by execution [1][6]. Community Impact (0/2): No company foundation, charitable program, or quantified community investment was found. Employee Retention (0/2): No retention data was found, and leadership has turned over repeatedly - Deanna White became interim CEO in May 2024 and permanent CEO in December 2024 after the prior CEO's exit [6]. Insider Buying (0/2): FMP shows four insider purchases in Q4 2024 and one in Q1-Q2 2025, but six insider sales in Q2 2026 and no purchases over the last 12 months - net selling [7].

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on available growth-sleeve metrics (6 weight units, weighted sum 2.92). Shareholders' equity is negative, so FMP reports D/E of -212%, which scores 0 because negative equity is worse than the 300% floor; ROE is not meaningful with negative equity and negative earnings and is excluded as null [4]. Forward P/E is negative (-0.13) and scores 0; the -101.6% profit margin scores 0 [3]. Revenue growth of 7.6% YoY scores 0.92 [3]. The revenue CAGR of 73.4% (FY2021 $11.8M to FY2025 $106.6M, a 4-year CAGR derived from FMP statements because FY2020 data is unavailable) scores 1.0 at 2x weight, but it is almost entirely acquisition-driven [4]. Forward PEG is not meaningful with losses and is excluded. Average daily dollar volume of about $3.3M (4.4M shares x $0.75) clears the $1M liquidity floor, but the sub-$1 share price creates NYSE listing-compliance risk.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): Surf Air flies people and cargo on physical aircraft under FAA Part 135/121 certificates; AI cannot substitute for that service, and no analyst flags AI displacement of commuter aviation [1]. The risk is long-dated - autonomy and AI-driven pilot automation could eventually erode the crewed regional model, and AI-optimized competitors in charter brokerage could compress take rates. AI Opportunity (0/1): SurfOS is being positioned as an AI-enabled software product with Palantir support for 2026 commercial rollout, but no AI revenue has been reported, so the tiebreaker point is not awarded [5][6].

infinite_game.summary: Surf Air articulates an ambitious vision of electrified, software-driven regional aviation, but its recent behavior is a survival game: route exits, cost cuts, a $110.6M FY2025 net loss, negative equity, and repeated leadership change. Sinek would see a company that may yet find its cause but is currently playing to reach the next financing rather than to keep playing indefinitely.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): The vision of accessible, sustainable regional air travel is articulated, but strategy has shifted from membership flying to scheduled commuter service to charter and software within a few years, and the electrification promise remains unproven [1][6]. The cause has not yet shaped consistent decisions through a full cycle.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): The company has had multiple CEO transitions since its 2023 listing, a co-founder lawsuit alleging he was pushed out, and ongoing restructuring and route exits [6][8]. No Glassdoor or engagement data was found to offset these signs of organizational instability.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Management commentary focuses on its own profitability path, SurfOS, and charter growth; no evidence was found of framing rivals such as Wheels Up or JSX as benchmarks that sharpen its offering [2].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Surf Air has repeatedly adapted its model - acquiring Southern Airways, pivoting toward charter (+101% YoY in Q2 2026), exiting unprofitable routes, and building SurfOS as a potential software business [2][5]. These pivots look driven more by financial necessity than by a guiding cause, so they earn partial credit.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Leadership has walked away from unprofitable scheduled routes, accepting near-term revenue loss to improve unit economics, and continues to fund SurfOS development during losses [2][5]. That is a real, costly choice, but it is also forced by a cash-constrained balance sheet.

investment_thesis: Surf Air offers a high-risk turnaround with real top-line momentum: Q2 2026 revenue of $29.5M was at the top of guidance, up 8% YoY and 15% sequentially, with charter revenue up about 101% [2]. Management reaffirmed FY2026 revenue of $128-138M (20-30% growth) and cut its adjusted EBITDA loss guidance to $25-30M, roughly a 40% improvement from its earlier outlook, and guided Q3 to $35.5-37.5M revenue with only a $4-7M adjusted EBITDA loss [2]. At a ~$100M market cap and roughly 0.9x sales, any credible path to EBITDA breakeven plus SurfOS commercialization with Palantir could re-rate the shares sharply [4][5].
thesis_continued: The bear case is balance-sheet survival. Shareholders' equity is negative, the current ratio is 0.26, working capital is -$116M, and FMP shows TTM free cash flow of roughly -$0.67 per share against a $0.75 stock price [4]. The Q2 2026 net loss was $28.1M and the FY2025 net loss $110.6M on $106.6M revenue, so further dilutive equity raises are likely [2][4]. The stock trades below $1, creating NYSE listing-compliance risk and possible reverse-split dilution, and electrification remains years from certification. Leadership turnover and a co-founder lawsuit add governance risk [6][8].
key_catalysts: Q3 2026 results versus guidance of $35.5-37.5M revenue and a $4-7M adjusted EBITDA loss, testing the path to breakeven
SurfOS commercial rollout with Palantir in 2026, producing the first third-party software revenue
Continued charter growth (+101% YoY in Q2 2026) and margin gains from exiting unprofitable scheduled routes
key_risks: Negative equity, a 0.26 current ratio, and ongoing cash burn make further dilutive financing or restructuring likely
Sub-$1 share price exposes the stock to NYSE listing deficiency and reverse-split risk
Electrification and SurfOS may fail to commercialize on schedule, leaving a low-margin commuter airline (FY2025 gross margin ~4%)
